chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The person who is afflicted with hardship is not in greater need of praying than the one who has been spared affliction but is not immune from it.

key_terms.المُعَافَى: The one spared / The healthy one

ai.seo_question: Why should healthy and safe people continue to make du'a?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual vulnerability of the 'Mu'afa' (the spared), arguing that their lack of immediate suffering can breed complacency, making them equally in need of supplication as those enduring active trials. This insight underscores the Shia concept of *Husn al-Zann* (good expectation) coupled with *Tawaqqu'* (anticipation of change), urging believers to maintain constant vigilance through prayer regardless of their current state of ease or hardship.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 302. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
The person who is afflicted with hardship is not in greater need of praying than the one who has been spared affliction but is not immune from it.
